source_text: Λογίσασθε δ᾿ ὅτι ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ταῦτα ἔφημεν ἐκ τοῦ ἐφ᾿ ἡμῖν εἶναι ἀρνεῖσθαι ἐξεταζομένους. Ἀλλ᾿ οὐ βουλόμεθα ζῆν ψευδολογοῦντες· τοῦ γὰρ αἰωνίου καὶ καθαροῦ βίου ἐπιθυμοῦντες τῆς μετὰ θεοῦ τοῦ πάντων πατρὸς καὶ δημιουργοῦ διαγωγῆς ἀντιποιούμεθα, καὶ σπεύδομεν ἐπὶ τὸ ὁμολογεῖν, οἱ πεπεισμένοι καὶ πιστεύοντες τυχεῖν τούτων δύνασθαι τοὺς τὸν θεὸν δι᾿ ἔργων πείσαντας, ὅτι αὐτῷ εἵποντο καὶ τῆς παρ᾿ αὐτῷ διαγωγῆς ἤρων, ἔνθα κακία οὐκ ἀντιτυπεῖ. Ὡς μὲν οὖν διὰ βραχέων εἰπεῖν, ἅ τε προσδοκῶμεν καὶ μεμαθήκαμεν διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ διδάσκομεν, ταῦτά ἐστι. Πλάτων δ᾿ ὁμοίως ἔφη Ῥαδάμανθυν καὶ Μίνω κολάσειν τοὺς ἀδίκους παρ᾿ αὐτοὺς ἐλθόντας· ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸ αὐτὸ πρᾶγμά φαμεν γενήσεσθαι, ἀλλ᾿ ὑπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, κἀν τοῖς αὐτοῖς σώμασι μετὰ τῶν ψυχῶν γινομένων καὶ αἰωνίαν κόλασιν κολασθησομένων, ἀλλ᾿ οὐχὶ χιλιονταετῆ περίοδον, ὡς ἐκεῖνος ἔφη, μόνον. Εἰ μὲν οὖν ἄπιστον ἢ ἀδύνατον τοῦτο φήσει τις, πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἥδε ἡ πλάνη ἐστὶν ἀλλ᾿ οὐ πρὸς ἕτερον, μέχρις οἷ ἔργῳ μηδὲν ἀδικοῦντες ἐλεγχόμεθα.
pass_a_gloss: Consider that we said these things on your behalf so that we, being examined, might deny what is upon us. But we do not wish to live speaking falsely; for we, desiring the eternal and pure life, are imitators of the conversation with God, the Father of all and Creator, and we hasten to confess, we who are convinced and believe that those who have persuaded God through works are able to obtain these things, that they followed Him and loved His conversation, where evil does not oppose. Therefore, to speak briefly, these are the things that we expect and have learned through Christ and teach. Plato also said that Rhadamanthus and Minos would punish the unjust who came to them; we say that the same thing will happen, but through Christ, and that in the same bodies, together with their souls, they will be punished with eternal punishment, but not a thousand-year period, as he said. If someone says that this is unbelievable or impossible, this error is against us, but not against another, until we, doing no wrong, are convicted by deed.
pass_b_english: Consider that we said these things on your behalf, because it is in our power to deny the charges when we are examined. Yet we do not wish to live by speaking falsely; for we, desiring the eternal and pure life, are imitators of the communion with God, the Father of all and Creator, and we hasten to confess. We are convinced and believe that those who have persuaded God through their works are able to obtain these things, because they followed Him and loved His communion, where evil does not stand against them. In short, these are the things we expect, have learned through Christ, and teach. Plato likewise said that Rhadamanthus and Minos would punish the unjust who came before them; we say the same thing will happen, but through Christ, and that in the same bodies together with their souls they will be punished with eternal punishment, not only a thousand-year period as he said. If someone declares this unbelievable or impossible, this error lies with us, not with another, until we are convicted by deed while doing no wrong.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex clause regarding the ability to deny charges (ἐκ τοῦ ἐφ᾿ ἡμῖν εἶναι ἀρνεῖσθαι), the imitation of God's conversation/communion (διαγωγῆς), and the distinction between the thousand-year period and eternal punishment. The reference to Plato is rendered faithfully.
